raw_segments.text: In our age, no man stops at faith, but every man goes further.
To inquire whether they arrive would perhaps be a piece of audacity.
On the other hand, it is surely a sign of breeding and culture that I assume every man
has faith, since otherwise it would be a strange way of speaking—that he goes further.
In those ancient days it was otherwise.
Then faith was a task for the whole of life, because it was assumed that the believing
facility is not acquired in days nor in weeks.
When then, the seasoned old man drew near to his end, having fought the good fight and
kept the faith, his heart was still young enough not to have forgotten that fear and
trembling which chastened the youth, which the man indeed mastered, but from which no
man wholly grows away, save in so far as he should succeed in going further as early as
Where those venerable figures arrived, in our age every man begins, in order to go further.
